Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health concerns, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

Industry observers note that 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

According to recent reports, 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

It has been revealed that 'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health complications at Birmingham City.

Recent findings suggest that the veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

It has been revealed that 'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he stated. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

According to recent reports, 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Industry observers note that speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he says. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

In a recent development, mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

Industry observers note that 'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood mentioned: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he indicates for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

Recent findings suggest that 'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring complications to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the firm man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

It has been revealed that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

Recent findings suggest that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

Sources indicate that they seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

According to recent reports, atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:03.

Liverpool's Premier League campaign resumes at Anfield on Sunday, when they take on fierce rivals Manchester United.

The hosts come into the clash in fourth place with 18 points after 10 matchweeks, whereas United are in 18th place with just eight points.

Andoni Iraola will know the importance of winning at Anfield considering he has already lost against Manchester City and Arsenal, and he cannot afford a loss against the Red Devils at their lowest moment.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Man United.

© Imago / David Rawcliffe, Propaganda Photo.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, though despite missing his side's win against Crystal Palace before the November international break, he could make his return against Man United.

© Iconsport / Marty Jean-Louis/Sipa USA.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

The right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him.".

Frimpong did not return before the break, but he could return to the squad against Man United.

In a recent development, possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City).

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some weeks, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Sources indicate that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The initiative was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one].".

The defender has since returned to parts of team training, though he is far behind the rest of the squad.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Much like Leoni, the right-back has returned to parts of team training, but Liverpool are set to take a cautious approach to his fitness.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

  • Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.
  • The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.

Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.

The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.

John McGlynn's Falkirk are the form team in the Scottish top flight over the past five games, and they will be confident of earning maximum points yet again on home turf.

The latest in their string of triumphs was a 5-2 demolition of last term's runners-up Hearts at Tynecastle Park, where the Bairns raced into a 4-0 lead by the half-time interval.

Bolstering the magnitude of McGlynn's side's feat further is the fact that thrashing followed a 2-0 win against Celtic, which itself marked a third consecutive clean sheet.

All in all, taking 15 points from the last 15 on offer has put Falkirk third in the Scottish Premiership, though their 21-point tally leaves them six behind second-placed Rangers and 10 short of top-of-the-table Celtic.

On the other hand, the Bairns are now four points clear of their seventh-placed opponents, and boasting the second-best defensive record in the division, McGlynn will be optimistic about his team's chances of seeing extending that advantage.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone earned promotion to the top flight by winning the Scottish Championship last term, and while plenty of sides have struggled with the step up in the past, Simo Valakari's men are in a strong position.

The Saints are right now seventh with 17 points after 13 games, level with sixth-placed Dundee United and fifth-placed Dundee.

Prior to the international break, Valakari's side downed the Dee 2-1, taking an early lead via Josh Campbell before Kai Fotheringham won the clash roughly 20 minutes from time.

That victory ended a four-game run without a win, though St Johnstone had only tasted defeat once during that stretch, and arrive with just a single loss from their last seven outings overall.

The visitors will be the underdogs on Saturday, but buoyed by their resilience - as well as having scored more goals (17) than any other team in the bottom half - they are sure to fight for the chance to climb into the top six.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

St Johnstone Scottish Premiership form:.

Falkirk will be without injured full-backs Ryan Strain and Leon McCann, though Jack McMillan and Scott Tanser should be on hand to start either side of centre-halves Lewis Neilson and Liam Henderson.

At the opposite end of the pitch, right wingers Aodhan Doherty and Joseph Gardner are dealing with respective foot and thigh injuries, while the left-sided Ethan Laidlaw and attacking midfielder Aidan Nesbitt have ankle concerns to contend with.

In their absence, Jacob Murrell looks set to start up top, supported by Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames.

As for St Johnstone, they have a generally fit squad, with centre-back Bozo Mikulic reportedly available after breaking his nose against Dundee just 14 minutes into his return from 20 months out with an ACL injury and a slew of problems in the aftermath.

Elsewhere, Joel Cotterill could operate alongside Jason Holt in the centre of the park, flanked by wing-backs Liam Smith and Josh Campbell.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Spencer, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

St Johnstone possible starting lineup:.

Steward; Diabate, Finlayson, Alic; Smith, Cotterill, Holt, Campbell; Steven, Schmidt, Fotheringham.

In the midst of more than just a purple patch, Falkirk have been immense of late, hammering Hearts, beating Celtic and maintaining a strong defensive record.

St Johnstone have proven their own resilience since making the step back up to the Premiership, but they will be hard-pressed to hold out against the division's form team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he mentioned with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

It has been revealed that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

Recent findings suggest that if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

It has been revealed that it is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

According to recent reports, they travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Sources indicate that tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are at the moment third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:29.

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain in the next winter transfer window. The Parisian club are ready to let him go on one condition.

According to recent reports, having joined PSG in the summer of 2025 from Lille for £34m (€40m), Lucas Chevalier has failed to make his mark at the Parisian club. While he was expected to succeed Gianluigi Donnarumma, he now finds himself as a mere understudy to Matvey Safonov.

According to recent reports, the Russian goalkeeper has won his place as first choice and is not letting go of it. Paris are very pleased with his performances and have reportedly even secretly wrapped up a contract extension. Safonov has played every game for the two-time European champions this season, leaving Lucas Chevalier without any game time.

It is a difficult situation for the French international, who missed the last World Cup and has not been called up by latest France manager Zinedine Zidane.

Already mentioned as a possible departure last summer, the former Lille man had chosen to stay. Canal+ reports that PSG had told him he would get a fresh chance if he kept working.

However, that chance never came. A point of no return appears to have been reached. ‘He wants to play, he needs to play. Today, his wish is to look elsewhere to find game time’ - Gauthier Kuntzmann revealed on the Late Football Club show. The Parisian club are ready to let him leave this winter.

In a recent development, ‘Paris Saint-Germain are aware that the situation of Lucas Chevalier cannot drag on. On top of that, he is losing market value and that is a factor, even if everything is going very well financially at PSG. 'I am telling you, Paris Saint-Germain do not rule out the idea, even in the short term, of seeing Lucas Chevalier leave on loan or in a sale, it will depend on the offers’ - Philippe Carayon explained on the same show.

Recent findings suggest that the task does not look simple for Lucas Chevalier. ‘Finding a goalkeeper position at a good club in January will not be simple. Except in the event of an injury at a club’ - Alain Roche warned. In any case, in this saga, PSG will only let their goalkeeper leave on one condition.

Sources indicate that ‘There will be an absolute prerequisite for Paris Saint-Germain, which is to find a top-level replacement for Safonov’ - Philippe Carayon stressed. That could complicate a departure for the French goalkeeper in January 2027 even further.

#26378. Latest Update: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1699 w)

Latest Update: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

#26377. Arsenal: Why Gunners and Havertz have so many offside problems

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1210 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal: Why Gunners and Havertz have so many offside problems

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:41.
  • In a recent development, arsenal have built a side capable of controlling matches and turning defensive consistency into results.
  • Sources indicate that according to Opta data, Arsenal have 35 offsides in the 2026-27 season, at least 11 more than any other side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:41.

In a recent development, arsenal have built a side capable of controlling matches and turning defensive consistency into results. Leaders of the Premier League, with nine wins in ten games, Mikel Arteta’s team appear to have few weaknesses. There is, however, one problem that stands out: the players are caught offside with unusual frequency, and Kai Havertz is at the centre of that statistic.

Sources indicate that according to Opta data, Arsenal have 35 offsides in the 2026-27 season, at least 11 more than any other side. The average of 3.5 per match is the highest for a team in a season since Hull City in 2008-09, with 3.7. The figure stands out even more when individual performance is considered: Havertz has been caught 15 times, almost double the second player in the ranking, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with eight.

Sources indicate that the number is not just a statistical curiosity. Every offside stops a move and wastes an attacking opportunity. But the explanation does not lie in a single factor. Arsenal’s style creates situations conducive to this type of infringement, opponents also play a part in the picture and, in Havertz’s case, there is a clear problem with the timing of his movements.

According to recent reports, the first explanation lies in how Arteta’s team occupy the pitch. Arsenal are a side that usually control possession, settle their players in the opposition half and circulate the ball until they find spaces to advance.

This territorial presence increases the number of situations in which the attackers can try to exploit the space behind the last line. When the ball reaches a player with room to lift his head, team-mates look to attack the depth, either to receive a vertical pass or to open space for those arriving from behind.

It has been revealed that it is a crucial movement for a team that frequently faces opponents in low blocks. If all the attackers waited for the ball to feet, Arsenal would have more difficulty disorganising compact defences. Attacking the space behind the centre-backs forces the opponent to make decisions: drop back to protect the area or push the line up to reduce the space between defence and midfield.

The problem is that the second alternative demands extra attention from the attackers. When the opposition defence advances in a coordinated way, the player starting the run must watch not only the ball but also the positions of the defenders. If he sets off before the pass, he can be offside even if he receives in good conditions.

Arsenal are third in the Premier League in ‘field tilt’, an indicator that measures the proportion of passes made in the attacking third relative to the total passes in the final thirds of the pitch, at 64.1%. They are also second for attempted through balls (31), passes ending in the attacking third (1,662) and passes that break the opposition defensive line (207).

In a recent development, in other words, the team create many situations in which their attackers can be found behind the defence. In addition, they have faced six of the sides that have most often caught opponents offside this season: Aston Villa, Coventry, Hull City, Leeds, Liverpool and Brighton. It is no coincidence that part of the numbers were built against opponents especially prepared to use this resource.

According to recent reports, the high line, therefore, helps explain the problem but is not enough to justify it. Manchester City and Tottenham, for example, have higher possession and territorial dominance figures, while Brighton also surpass Arsenal in passes that break the defence. Even so, Arsenal are clear leaders in offsides. There is also a sampling factor. Arsenal were caught eight times against Aston Villa in August, the most by a side in a single Premier League match in the past two and a half years.

According to recent reports, in just ten games, such an outlying match carries considerable weight in the average. But the seven offsides against Leeds, five against Coventry and four against Hull show it is not an isolated episode.

If collective behaviour explains part of the picture, Havertz’s situation stands out for another reason. The German has 15 offsides, a figure too high to be attributed only to the style of play or the characteristics of the opponents.

According to recent reports, there is a perception that Havertz, having played as a midfielder for much of his career, prefers to drop back to take part in build-up play. But the data show he also frequently looks to attack the space behind the defence. In the Premier League, he has made 125 high-intensity runs of this type, the third highest figure in the competition.

It has been revealed that gonzalo Garcia, of Fulham, made 145 of these runs and was caught offside only twice. Bryan Mbeumo, of Manchester United, made 141 and was flagged four times. Both have played at least 90 minutes more than Havertz.

This does not mean the German should stop attacking the depth. The question is the quality of execution. The attacker needs to identify the moment when his team-mate is ready to make the pass and adjust his sprint to the movement of the defence.

It has been revealed that offside can come down to centimetres. A forward who sets off too early loses the chance to receive legally, even if he has correctly identified the space. If he delays, he lets the defender recover and close the passing lane.

Some of Havertz’s moves this season look more avoidable. There are also situations in which the team need to improve collective coordination. Arsenal have had 11 offsides within 15 seconds of a set piece being taken. On two occasions, players were caught after long balls from goalkeeper David Raya. These are moves that demand attention from the attackers and better communication about when to attack the space.

According to recent reports, so far, the offsides have not stopped Arsenal building an excellent campaign. They lead the Premier League with 27 points, five clear of second place. Defensive solidity allows the team to win matches even when the attack does not produce a high volume of goals.

Recent findings suggest that but there is a possible side effect. Arsenal have scored only 15 times in the first ten games. At that rate, they would finish the season with 57 goals, which would be the lowest total in the history of a Premier League champion. The team can keep winning with their defensive organisation, but will hardly have the same safety margin if their rivals improve their attacking performance.

Recent findings suggest that the 35 offsides represent possessions interrupted before the move could reach its end. Not all would be clear goalscoring opportunities, but some could result in dangerous shots. In a tight race, wasting so many attacks can make a difference.

Arteta’s challenge is not to ask his players to stop attacking the depth. That would mean giving up an important tool for dismantling compact defences. The way forward is to improve coordination between the passer and the runner, as well as to guide the players better on how to react to the opposition defensive line.

  • Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.
  • Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but claims he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:48 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:41 EST, 17 November 2026.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but claims he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he said on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

It has been revealed that 'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He stated without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend said he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

Recent findings suggest that 'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

Industry observers note that 'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney remarked. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

Industry observers note that 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

According to recent reports, 'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

Recent findings suggest that 'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

Recent findings suggest that he previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

Sources indicate that he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

He also said part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

Industry observers note that 'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

Recent findings suggest that in his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

It has been revealed that 'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney said: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:07.

Mauricio Pochettino is keen to make significant behind-the-scenes changes at Manchester United following his arrival at Old Trafford.

The new Red Devils boss is understood to have identified a preferred candidate to replace sporting director Jason Wilcox, with whom he previously enjoyed a successful working relationship.

Paul Mitchell could now emerge as a leading contender for a return to football after previously being considered by INEOS.

According to reports, Pochettino has recommended Mitchell as United's next sporting director, believing the 45-year-old would be the ideal replacement for Wilcox.

The Argentine, who has signed a contract until June 2029, is noted to have made his concerns about Wilcox clear during discussions with the club hierarchy before accepting the managerial position.

Wilcox has come under scrutiny following United's disappointing recent form and questions over the quality and depth of the squad assembled during his time at the club.

Pochettino is keen to work with someone he trusts, having previously enjoyed productive spells alongside Mitchell at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Mitchell was reportedly considered by INEOS for a senior football position in October 2023, before Wilcox ultimately took the role in April 2024.

It has been revealed that the 45-year-old recruitment chief also held positions at RB Leipzig and Monaco before spending 11 months as Newcastle's sporting director between 2024 and 2025. He has been out of football since departing St James' Park.

There are legitimate questions over whether Wilcox has delivered enough to justify remaining in such an influential position at Old Trafford.

United's summer recruitment has left several important areas of the squad needing attention, particularly left-back and centre-forward, while the club have also struggled to generate funds by moving on unwanted players.

Marcus Rashford's situation is one example of the wider challenge of moving players who no longer fit the club's plans.

Furthermore, the decision to appoint Michael Carrick permanently before his eventual departure will inevitably come under scrutiny, especially given the responsibility placed on the sporting department to identify the right managerial appointment.

Mitchell would bring considerable recruitment experience and, crucially, an existing relationship with Pochettino.

INEOS should not make a change simply to satisfy a newly introduced manager, but if Wilcox has failed to provide the squad-building structure and recruitment strategy United need, replacing him could be a sensible step.

Pochettino needs a sporting director who shares his vision, and Mitchell could be a compelling candidate to help deliver that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

It has been revealed that as we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has substantial prepares to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The new ‘MSE’ holding manufacturer is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that it is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

According to recent reports, serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

In a recent development, “You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

“So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

“This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

According to recent reports, “Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

Recent findings suggest that “The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

Sources indicate that “This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

It has been revealed that “Building a great stadium like this is something extremely crucial. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this company that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

“So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this new stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this upcoming stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European company – but I would also say worldwide.

It has been revealed that “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the new stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

“Naturally, as always with these issues, there may be some discussion points. Furthermore, in Milan we’re heading towards an election campaign for a new mayor, and a topic like the construction of a new stadium is one that can naturally excite politicians.

According to recent reports, “Let’s say we’re confident because the entire process we’ve taken so far protects us from these potential disruptions, and we’re fiercely determined to move forward. With the fresh stadium, among other things, we’ll have €100 million in additional revenue.

“This €100 million in additional revenue is a fundamental ingredient for the success of AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Serie A around the world, because ultimately, €100 million – to have great players, to pay great players – is a fundamental ingredient for success.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 07:20.

Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.

With just seven points to their name from their opening nine Bundesliga matches, Union Berlin are already feeling the pressure.

Head coach Mauro Lustrinelli survived the international break, with the club's hierarchy seemingly prepared to give the Swiss tactician more time to turn things around.

However, his long-term future remains far from certain, particularly after director Horst Heldt cast doubt over whether the 47-year-old would still be in charge over the next five months.

Heldt also revealed that Union are already drawing up plans for the January transfer window, although with more than a month to go before it opens, any potential reinforcements are unlikely to provide Lustrinelli with immediate relief.

What may help the Swiss coach is the fact Union’s best results this season have come at home, with 86% of all their points coming at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Nevertheless, Union's defensive problems overshadow any slight positives, given they have already conceded 21 goals - a newly introduced club record at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign.

While Union struggle to keep the ball out of the net, RB Leipzig simply cannot stop scoring at the moment.

Martin Demichelis and his men have already rattled the net 27 times in the Bundesliga this season - a total only bettered by Bayern Munich, who have scored on 29 occasions.

Just before the international break, Leipzig put five goals past Augsburg in a 5-2 victory - a game which extended their winning run to three straight league matches.

In recent times, Leipzig have also seen an upswing in their away results, winning their last two competitive games on the road - including a 2-0 success against Schalke at the end of October.

Striking early has been the key for Die Rotten Bullen so far this season, with the club yet to drop a point when scoring first in the Bundesliga.

In fact, the only major concern ahead of Saturday’s game is the fact Leipzig have lost four of their last six trips to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Union Berlin form (all competitions):.

RB Leipzig form (all competitions):.

French defender Stanley Nsoki has missed every game this season for Union Berlin due to a muscle injury, and the 27-year-old will remain on the sidelines this weekend.

Robert Skov has only played one competitive minute this term, though he has recently returned to individual training.

Youngster Andrik Markgraf also remains out of action due to a knee injury, while Janik Haberer could miss Saturday’s game through illness.

When it comes to RB Leipzig, the visitors are also dealing with a handful of injuries as we head towards the end of the calendar year.

German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo has been out of action since September with a shoulder problem.

Youngsters Viggo Gebel and Marc Guiu are also dealing with knee and hamstring injuries.

Max Finkgrafe, meanwhile, has missed his last five games with a thigh injury, but is on the brink of a return.

Antonio Nusa, who has 11 goal contributions in nine Bundesliga games this season, is the man to watch for the visitors.

Union Berlin possible starting lineup:.

Ronnow; Juranovic, Van den Bosch, Friedrich, Rothe; Imeri, Schafer, Khedira, Aebischer; Ilic, Burke.

RB Leipzig possible starting lineup:.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; El Aynaoui, Banzuzi; Gruda, Nkunku, Nusa; Romulo.

Union Berlin perform a lot better at home, but that may not be enough to stop a rampant RB Leipzig side that simply cannot stop scoring goals.

The visitors smell blood as they continue to chase the top two, and there is a strong possibility that things could get ugly in Berlin.

Xabi Alonso's January transfer initiative dealt cruel blow as Chelsea 'barred' from signing £30m maestro

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (404 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32.
  • Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.
  • The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32.

Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.

The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Juventus are determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger, with a potential departure presently considered off the table.

Alajbegovic was pursued by Chelsea during the summer after impressing at RB Salzburg, but the west London club's proposed project failed to convince the youngster.

The Blues were understood to be considering sending him out on loan rather than offering immediate first-team opportunities, allowing the Serie A giants to secure his signature instead.

There has now been renewed interest from Alonso's side, but reports in Italy (via Sport Witness) suggest Chelsea face an uphill battle to bring the 19-year-old maestro to Stamford Bridge.

It is claimed that Alajbegovic 'isn't leaving' Juventus, with the Italian side pleased by his development and unwilling to consider an exit despite interest from England.

The £30m teenager is also happy with his role in Turin, where he believes he has the right environment to continue developing, with similar reports suggesting that he wants to remain at Juventus for a 'long time'.

As a result, an immediate departure has been described as 'truly barred', making a January transfer particularly difficult to negotiate.

Chelsea's interest is understandable given the Bosnian's potential, but the club may struggle to convince him that Stamford Bridge is the right place for his development.

Regular first-team football should be a priority for a teenager at this stage of his career, and Juventus are presently providing him with opportunities to establish himself.

By contrast, Chelsea's sizeable squad creates greater competition for attacking positions, with even highly-rated youngster Estevao having experienced his own difficulties securing consistent game time.

That situation could serve as a warning to Alajbegovic, particularly when he is already enjoying an increasingly prominent role in Turin.

Although Juventus may not offer the most stable environment, they are giving the youngster opportunities to develop at senior level.

Chelsea might be able to offer a lucrative project, but unless they can guarantee a clearer pathway into the first team, Alajbegovic would arguably be better off remaining in Italy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

Industry observers note that the newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter. Part of the reason for this is because Endrick – the alternative name – made his intentions clear: “I hope to spend my life at Real Madrid.”.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that in this story of preferences, Tresoldi’s choice is also crucial. The 22-year-old has supported Milan since he was a child, while in Belgium and beyond he has proven himself to be a goal scorer. Inter found this out, as he scored a hat-trick against them in the Champions League at San Siro.

The No.9 shirt and role is currently occupied by Gonçalo Ramos, not a trivial thing due to the record-breaking fee paid for him last summer. However, Ruben Amorim genuinely believes the Portuguese can co-exist with Tresoldi, who can be on hand to finish the chances created by Ramos’ movement.

Sources indicate that tresoldi is a true ‘devil’ in the penalty area. He has 18 goals this season for club (eight in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Belgian Super Cup) and another four for Germany’s U21s. This leaves him just shy of 20 goals, in mid-November.

Tresoldi is also desperate to move to Milan and if it were up to him, the deal would be done. His desire to join his boyhood club could prove helpful and provide a boost to the deal’s success, just as it has before. His agents and family are equally positive about a potential Italian move.

Club Brugge are in a different mood, however, and would happily keep him unless offered at least €60m. Just a few months ago, the Belgian giants rejected offers just over half that. This is a figure Milan are willing to negotiate around, because Champions League qualification is crucial and goals are needed to achieve this.

Industry observers note that besides, Cardinale is of the opinion that it’s better to invest now than risk deepening the deficit. Another year without the revenues from the top club competition would be far from ideal for many different reasons.

What about Francesco Camarda? Here too, the debate is over: the club and the coach agree on the need for a loan, perhaps abroad. Camarda agrees: he knows he needs to regain rhythm by playing regularly, to help his development.

In a recent development, for Milan, it would be another negotiation with Brugge after Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. The deal for the former was conducted by Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara, while for the latter it was Igli Tare. Now, Cardinale intends to do things himself.

The owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

#26356. Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

📅 14 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.
  • In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes.
  • According to recent reports, city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

According to recent reports, city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Sources indicate that could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

According to recent reports, the data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In a recent development, in the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

Industry observers note that it could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] remarked at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

Did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H.

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

It has been revealed that so we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

In a recent development, then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Sources indicate that then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG's lead just 2 minutes after they scored the first 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/MxhJ3oCWpC.

After Achraf Hakimi headed against the inside of a post and City could not clear, the ball came back with Warren Zaïre-Emery flicking on Maghnes Akliouche’s cut-back. It ran to Vitinha who slammed in a first-time shot. It was the first time City had ever conceded three goals at home in the first half of this competition.

Vitinha with a BEAUTY to put PSG three up after just 30 minutes 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/vgqkI6kI3h.

Industry observers note that maybe it was too easy. Maybe City could not continue to be so dominated but it was as if a switch was flicked when the teams returned. The chances came for City. Enzo Fernández should have scored from a close-range header and Haaland did, glancing in an inswinging Ndiaye cross.

Finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

But City did not stop. Nuno Mendes headed Josko Gvardiol’s flick off the line, Fernández hit a post before Bouaddi set up Haaland and he swept the ball past Safonov.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

There was time for PSG to miss a penalty, with Donnarumma comfortably saving Ferran Torres’s weak effort as City bravely continued to push. They lost, but it did not quite feel like that.

According to recent reports, I think our start was quite good until the first goal. Then we conceded the second after one [more] minute and that created bad feelings so we struggled.

Second half we were much, much, much better and we probably deserved even something more.

According to recent reports, it was strange to be honest because until the first goal we were in the game. We created things, didn’t concede and then the first goal led to the second one. When you concede two goals in two minutes it could [get] even worse.

Industry observers note that at half-time we adjust something, didn’t lose our balance and in the second half we created enough to deserve something more. We adjusted the way we were pressing, something on the ball [too].

We lost the balance [by conceding the second goal]. Even at zero-three we created enough in the second half and Luis said afterwards that they had been quite lucky.

It has been revealed that [A message for the fans?] We feel sorry for the first half but I think we’re quite happy now. Major game on Saturday [Ipswich at home at 3pm].

Industry observers note that both Arsenal and Barcelona had shorter prices than PSG to win the Champions League. Now it’s only Barcelona but I would say even they are not as good as PSG.

I doubt Guardiola will speak publicly but let’s wait and see.

FT: Manchester City 2-4 PSG #UCL | @bet365 | 18+ | #AD https://t.co/fPdGHP2OHp.

According to recent reports, matheus Nunes, Bouaddi and Ndiaye were terrific. Small wonder that Luis Enrique and Maresca were exhaling hard as they embraced at the final whistle.

After a PSG performance in the first half that was as good as any I’ve seen in the past 10 years, Manchester City stiffened midfield in the second and went toe-to-toe to play their part in a basketball game with crosses and shots raining down on the PSG goal.

PSG have managed this last few minutes well, making vital tackles and interceptions.

Pacho cuts out a pass to stop Semenyo pouncing.

City have had 27 attempts on goal, PSG 14.

PSG have dropped back in numbers and City are probing away.

Recent findings suggest that four minutes to come. O’Reilly replaces Enzo Fernandez.

Sources indicate that ferran Torres hit it low and not even halfway towards the right post. Terrible penalty, straightforward save.

Sources indicate that his hand touched the sole of his boot as he slid in. Very soft.

Didn’t seen that Matheus Nunes touched Nuno Mendes from the replay.

Semenyo takes Haaland’s pass and his iffy control by the right of the penalty spot knocks it up. He does well to manipulate the defender out of the way but the ball won’t come down quick enough and he ends up stretching for it and lashes it over the bar.

Anderson, looking for Haaland from the left with a right-foot inswinger, overcooks it and Safonov comes off his line to catch.

Haaland meets Nunes daisycutter of a cross having been sent to the byline with his outstretched left leg as he slides in at the back post and Safonov sprawls to save on the goalline again. Should have scored but then again he was right at the extent of his reach when he made the connection.
