When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Recent findings suggest that both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the upcoming order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

According to recent reports, whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

According to recent reports, after Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Recent findings suggest that having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

PSG have made a slow start to their Ligue 1 campaign, their worst since Luis Enrique’s first season in charge. Starting with two draws and a defeat, they have rallied with three successive victories to climb up to sixth as the head coach, as he tends to do in the league, rotates his midfielders and forwards like crazy, to whose ranks he has added the World Cup-winner Ferran Torres. The summer signing scored a hat-trick in his Champions League debut for the club, a 6-1 mauling of Slovan Bratislava.

City, too, started their European campaign with a win, Erling Haaland scoring both goals in the 2-0 victory over Porto at the Dragao and you won’t need me to remind you that they have won all six of their Premier League games to lead Arsenal by three points at the top of the table.

  • Tottenham Hotspur are considering a 'surprise' move for Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his attacking options.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a 'surprise' move for Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The 23-year-old has revived his career at the City Ground following a difficult spell at Chelsea, attracting renewed interest from north London.

However, a potential deal could be more complicated than initially expected, with Forest placing a substantial valuation on their summer signing.

According to FootballTransfers, Delap is 'admired' by De Zerbi, with Spurs continuing to monitor the former Ipswich Town forward after tracking him during the summer transfer window.

Delap has scored three goals in his first nine Premier League appearances for Forest, offering encouraging signs following his disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge.

A January move is considered extremely difficult, though, given Forest only signed him in the summer and are unlikely to sanction his departure while fighting for their Premier League status.

Tricky Trees owner Evangelos Marinakis is not expected to approve a mid-season sale, although it is understood that De Zerbi could be prepared to wait until the summer of 2027.

Forest are likely to demand around £75m for the Englishman, which would represent a significant profit on the initial £45m they paid Chelsea.

There is no denying that Delap has shown some improvement at Forest, but his overall Premier League goalscoring record remains a significant concern amid Spurs' renewed interest.

His three goals this season take his career total to just 16 efforts in 76 Premier League outings, while he managed only three goals in 47 appearances for Chelsea.

Those numbers hardly suggest a striker capable of immediately resolving Tottenham's attacking problems, particularly if Forest demand £75m to part with him.

Spurs still need a reliable source of goals if they are to climb the table and compete for major honours, rather than another expensive gamble on potential.

De Zerbi's admiration is understandable, but Tottenham should be wary of paying a premium for a forward whose top-flight returns remain underwhelming.

Delap may yet develop into an excellent striker, but spending that much on him would represent a considerable risk for a club with more pressing needs.

Chelsea's Malo Gusto named 'biggest disappointment of the Zidane era'... and Liverpool's £123m man Bradley Barcola 'lacked accuracy and composure' in damning verdict on France's Premier League stars

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:01 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under latest coach Zinedine Zidane.
  • Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 06:01 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 17 November 2026.

The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under latest coach Zinedine Zidane.

Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.

And among the team's most glaring underperformers – according to some observers in France – were Chelsea's Malo Gusto, Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Liverpool's £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola.

French outlet RMC Sport was particularly critical of the pair, with journalist Alexandre Jaquin describing Gusto as 'probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era'.

Jaquin added: 'Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

Malo Gusto struggled has been under fire from the French media after a string of poor performances under Zinedine Zidane.

The honeymoon period is over for Zidane, according to French media.

Recent findings suggest that 'Overwhelmed by his opponents' energy and little helped by Michael Olise's lack of defensive defense, the former Lyon player lived a nightmare in Lombardy, notably conceding a penalty. A match quickly erased from his memory.'.

In a recent development, RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

Industry observers note that 'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'.

Industry observers note that even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin said: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'.

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season.

Journalist Walid Acherchour made his feelings known on the After Foot programme, saying: 'Zidane hit a wall of reality with this second international break... I found the attitude of some individuals against Turkey to be very poor.

'In the second half against Italy and in the match against Turkey, how do you manage without the ball when you're being torn apart in midfield? Zidane will have to work on all these questions.'.

Acherchour closed by saying bluntly: 'The honeymoon is over.'.

After an ultimately disappointing World Cup in which the French were again by Spain in a major semi-final – following their Euro 2024 exit – long-term manager Didier Deschamps left after 14 years in charge.

Legendary midfielder Zidane succeeded him in the summer and has already led France to the top of their Nations League group – but some of his players may have to go much further to win over their critics.

Schalke 04 vs Stuttgart - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 08:09.
  • Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga will come from the Veltins Arena in Gelsenkirchen, as Schalke 04 welcome Stuttgart for a tasty league encounter.
  • The hosts have endured a dreadful start to the season and are still looking to score their first home goal, while the visitors are setting their sights on a third successive league success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 08:09.

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga will come from the Veltins Arena in Gelsenkirchen, as Schalke 04 welcome Stuttgart for a tasty league encounter.

The hosts have endured a dreadful start to the season and are still looking to score their first home goal, while the visitors are setting their sights on a third successive league success.

Schalke ended their five-match goalless run last time out against Hoffenheim, although their attacking breakthrough counted for little as they suffered a 2-1 defeat.

That result left Die Konigsblauen sitting in the relegation zone during the international break, while head coach Miron Muslic avoided an early sack.

Nevertheless, the 44-year-old remains under considerable pressure, with Schalke now enduring a seven-game winless streak across all competitions.

Even more concerning for the Royal Blues faithful is the fact that their points tally after nine Bundesliga matches is identical to the one they recorded at the same stage of their disastrous 2022-23 campaign, which ended in relegation.

In order to turn things around, the hosts will need to start scoring goals, otherwise they risk becoming just the second team in Bundesliga history to go without a goal across their first five home matches of a season.

There is one positive for the hosts and that is the fact they beat Stuttgart when these two teams last met back in February 2023 - their only victory over the Swabians in five previous meetings.

While Schalke are on the ropes, Stuttgart are on the attack, with the Swabians looking to record their third straight Bundesliga win.

Sebastian Hoeness and his side powered to a 1-0 win over Werder Bremen just before the international break, leaving them just six points adrift of the top four.

Given their sluggish start to the campaign, Stuttgart's recent upturn represents a welcome change in fortunes, with their defensive improvements playing a significant role.

Two clean sheets from their last three domestic outings make for much better reading than the two shutouts they managed across their opening 10 matches of the season.

Stuttgart will now turn their attention to landing their first league win over Schalke since 2021 - the only success over the Royal Blues they boast in 12 previous meetings.

What’s more, the Swabians have not managed to win at the Veltins Arena since 2013 - losing four and drawing three of their last seven trips to Gelsenkirchen.

Schalke 04 form (all competitions):.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Along with their goalscoring problems, Schalke are also dealing with a lengthy injury list.

Maximilian Wober and youngster Luca Vozar are both currently out with hamstring injuries.

Defender Timo Becker picked up a foot problem just before the international break, and will also remain on the sidelines.

Emil Hojlund is yet to feature for Schalke this season due to an Achilles injury, while midfielder Ron Schallenberg is out with a leg problem.

Stuttgart are also missing a handful of names, including midfielder Angelo Stiller who is struggling with an adductor injury.

Swiss defender Luca Jaquez featured in the 1-0 win over Bremen before the international break, but he has since become a doubt due to a ribs problem.

Youngsters Jarzinho Malanga and Justin Diehl complete the injury list, with the two players carrying thigh and abdominal issues.

Meanwhile, forward Deniz Undav missed out on selection for the German national team, with the 30-year-old still looking for his first Bundesliga goal this season.

Schalke 04 possible starting lineup:.

Karius; Ayhan, Katic, Kurucay, V. Becker; El-Faouzi, Tanaka; Ljubicic, Karaman, Aouchiche; Hwang.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Seimen; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; El Khannouss, Undav; Demirovic.

Schalke are simply not scoring at home, and they could struggle here against an improving Stuttgart defence.

The visitors have struggled away in Gelsenkirchen over the years, but this is the perfect opportunity to improve that record.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:12.

Bruno Fernandes will be bidding to inspire Manchester United to a huge victory when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

The match will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first fixture in charge of the 20-time English champions, and he will be hoping for inspiration from his captain.

Fernandes has found it difficult to show his best form for the Red Devils this season, but the 32-year-old has still managed to come up with six goals and three assists in 14 appearances.

Here, Sports Mole looks at how the Portugal international has performed against Liverpool during his professional career.

Fernandes has faced Liverpool on 13 previous occasions during his professional career, boasting a record of five wins, three draws and five defeats.

The attacker has scored three times against the Reds, in addition to contributing two assists.

Eleven of Fernandes' appearances against Liverpool have come in the Premier League, boasting a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats, scoring twice and registering two assists.

Fernandes has also faced Liverpool twice in the FA Cup, helping Man United to record a 3-2 win in the fourth round of the competition in 2021, finding the back of the net, before playing in a 4-3 success for the Red Devils in the quarter-finals in March 2024.

The Portuguese's two Premier League goals against Liverpool have been at Old Trafford, so he would create some personal history by finding the back of the net at Anfield on Sunday.

Last season, Fernandes provided an assist in a 2-1 Man United win at Anfield, before helping the Red Devils record a 3-2 victory in the reverse game at Old Trafford.

Christian Pulisic revealed his emotions after scoring a brilliant bicycle kick during the USA’s final game under Mauricio Pochettino.

It was known before the USMNT’s two-legged UEFA Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti that it would be Pochettino’s last two games, given that he has an agreement in place to take over the job at Manchester United vacated following Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The stars and stripes certainly gave him a fitting send-off, as they won the first leg 6-0 a few days ago and then completed the job with a 2-0 victory in Cincinnati last night. Pulisic got the first goal after a brace in the previous rout, and it was an incredible overhead kick.

Pulisic was actually overlooked by Pochettino for the September-October window – partly for fitness reasons – and he spoke to reporters after the game to share his thoughts after an emotional evening. He was called the ‘best player on the pitch’ by the US media, and his words are via MilanNews.

An overhead kick goal is pretty special….

“I’ve never scored a goal like that, it was special. Weston crossed the ball and it was the only thing I could really do, so I thought I had to give it a try. It was really nice to see the ball go in.”.

Is it nice to get a victory on Pochettino’s farewell day?

“Yes, obviously he’s leaving now, so it’s nice to end with a good performance and a nice win for the team.”.

How would you describe this particular group, a mix of veterans and young players?

“It’s really nice. It’s been fun working with everyone. We got to meet some of the upcoming guys, even some young talent, and obviously there’s still some of the same core group, so it’s a really great team. I really like where we are right now and I think we’re still growing and have a great future ahead of us.”.

What does Pochettino’s last match leave you with?

Industry observers note that “We’re in a good place. Overall, I think the team has improved. I think there’s a good culture within the group, and I think we should be really excited about the future.”.

What kind of an impact has Julian Hall made?

Sources indicate that “It was fantastic playing with him. He scored a goal, but also just for his overall play, making lots of runs and causing problems for the other team. He did a great job, fitting in with this team and making his mark.”.

What was Mauricio Pochettino’s farewell message to you this evening?

According to recent reports, “Simply that we have a truly extraordinary culture. We’ve built something truly special and that a bright future awaits us. And to continue that by letting the rest of the team support us.”.

Does it really matter who the coach is at this point?

According to recent reports, “I mean, not that it doesn’t matter. Ultimately, it’s not our choice, as players. We hope whoever arrives will be able to capitalise on the things we do so well and lead us in the right direction.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:12, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:14.

Manchester City and Fulham will continue their respective Premier League campaigns with a contest at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts are third in the Premier League table, six points behind the leaders Arsenal, while Fulham are down in 15th spot in the division on 10 points.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 12.30pm UK time on Saturday.

The Premier League match between Man City and Fulham will be played at the Etihad Stadium.

The corresponding game last season ended in a 3-0 win for the Citizens, while Fulham have not beaten Man City in any competition since a league clash in April 2009.

The Premier League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.20pm and run until 11.45pm, with highlights of the match also available via that avenue.

Man City have lost each of their last three Premier League matches to Aston Villa, Brighton & Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest, which has seen them lose vital ground in the title race.

Enzo Maresca's side must bounce back on Saturday to avoid the possibility of Arsenal pulling further clear at the summit, as the Gunners could prove incredibly difficult to catch.

Man City have won each of their last 20 matches against Fulham in all competitions - a remarkable run - but their last three losses to the London club have come on home soil.

Fulham are unbeaten in their last four Premier League matches, and they picked up a point in a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa in their last away league fixture.

Man City dare not suffer another defeat or it could spell serious trouble for their title ambitions.

Declan Rice has agreed a fresh five-year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031 - with goalkeeper David Raya set to join him in committing his future to the club.

The England midfielder is expected to sign the fresh contract soon, which is set to put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Saka is on a deal worth over £350,000 a week.

And Raya, 31, is understood to have agreed a deal in principle to extend his terms. Both players' existing deals expire in 2028.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105million from West Ham and has established himself as the fulcrum of their midfield, helping steer them to the Premier League title last season.

The 27-year-old played 55 games in all competitions last season as the Gunners reached their first Champions League final since 2006, but lost out to Paris Saint-Germain.

His contract talks have been ongoing from at least March and are now finalised.

Raya joined Arsenal from Brentford on loan in the same summer, and signed a permanent deal a year later.

Declan Rice has agreed a latest-five year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031.

David Raya has agreed a deal in principle to stay on, with his current deal expiring in 2028.

Rice had confirmed a latest deal was close over the weekend when speaking on international duty with England.

'I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career.

'I've always been stable in the clubs I've been at.

'A latest contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

'I'm extremely lucky that I'm at a club like Arsenal, where my manager [Mikel Arteta] and my team-mates put so much energy in me.

'I'm extremely lucky I don't have to think about that stuff.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.
  • Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.
  • Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” mentioned Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Recent findings suggest that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Sources indicate that palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Industry observers note that bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Recent findings suggest that brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:14, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:15.

Newcastle United will welcome Arsenal to St James' Park in the Premier League on Saturday evening.

Newcastle are 12th in the Premier League table, boasting 12 points from their opening 10 matches of the season, while Arsenal are at the head of the division, five points ahead of second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 5.30pm UK time on Saturday.

The Premier League match between Newcastle and Arsenal will be held at the former's home ground, St James' Park.

The corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 victory for Arsenal, with Mikel Merino and Gabriel scoring late to secure all three points for the North London outfit.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.20pm and run until 11.45pm, with highlights of the match also available via that avenue.

Arsenal have won nine and lost one of their 10 Premier League matches this season, with 27 points leaving them five points clear at the top of the division.

Mikel Arteta's side recorded a 1-0 win over Hull City before the November international break, and they have been victorious in their last three matches in all competitions.

The likes of Brighton and Man City will be hoping for a favour from Newcastle in this match, as Arsenal are threatening to pull further clear at the top of the division.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough start to the season for Newcastle, with 12 points leaving them down in 12th spot in the division.

The Magpies entered the November international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Latest Update: Nations League quarter-final draw: Why England are favourites to win the tournament

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.
  • England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.
  • Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

It has been revealed that asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

Sources indicate that “It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

“Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

In a recent development, "With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

Industry News: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open latest opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

Recent findings suggest that a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

Recent findings suggest that a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

Industry observers note that a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

According to recent reports, a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

Recent findings suggest that a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

Latest Update: Gary Neville introduces surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.
  • The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the newly introduced manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

Industry observers note that 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

In a recent development, '(De Ligt has) got one big problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

In a recent development, 'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

In a recent development, 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

Recent findings suggest that 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in upcoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come swiftly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

Sources indicate that 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

It has been revealed that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

It has been revealed that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

According to recent reports, ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Bologna vs Udinese - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 09:03, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:08.
  • Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.
  • After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's upcoming boss has sparked a surge up the standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 09:03, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:08.

Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.

After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's upcoming boss has sparked a surge up the standings.

Since Raffaele Palladino's arrival midway through September, Bologna have been a team transformed, winning five games from six and climbing towards the European places.

The Emilian club signed off for the international break with a run of four consecutive wins, with the highlight being a 4-2 victory over AC Milan at San Siro.

Last time out, the Rossoblu's revival continued in the Derby dell'Emilia against Parma, as their hosts were swiftly reduced to 10 men and ultimately suffered a 2-1 defeat.

So, having won none of their first five games during the short-lived Domenico Tedesco era, Bologna are now one of Serie A's form sides.

However, Palladino must still work on their awful home record, which stretches back through most of last season; so far this term, they have claimed five points from a possible 15 at the Dall'Ara.

Either home or away, Udinese have picked up just one from their last nine matches and are therefore stuck at the foot of the table.

The Bianconeri have put a meagre five points on the board so far, slumping into an unexpected crisis.

Safe mid-table finishers in back-to-back seasons under Kosta Runjaic, this campaign has completely unravelled, and even a change of coach has yet to produce results.

Just before the break, latest boss Paolo Zanetti lost his first game against former club Venezia, with Udinese going down 2-1 in a crucial battle at the bottom.

Now, desperately needing some success, Zanetti must meet Palladino for the seventh time in management - to date, the pair have three wins apiece.

Unfortunately for fans of the Friulani, recent history is not on their side: they have won none of the last five meetings with Bologna, failing to even score in each of the last three.

Though Bologna will be without injured trio Jay Enem, Juan Miranda and Emil Holm, left-winger Nicolo Cambiaghi has resumed training after leaving Italy's UEFA Nations League camp.

Having impressed in the Azzurri's win over France, Cambiaghi has overcome a minor ankle problem and should start alongside Federico Bernadeschi in the final third.

The latter has previously scored four goals against Udinese, finding the net as a substitute in both of the last two meetings.

Bernardeschi and Samuel Mbangula - who recently hit a hat-trick at San Siro - are the hosts' joint-top Serie A scorers with three goals each; Jurgen Ekkelenkamp has netted three times for Udinese.

The visitors must travel without Nicolo Bertola, who has suffered a thigh injury in training and joins Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines.

In better news for Zanetti, David Alaba could return from his latest layoff, while Nicolo Zaniolo is available after withdrawing from the Italy squad for personal reasons.

Set to support Keinan Davis up front, Zaniolo has played eight league games against Bologna without ever scoring.

Bologna possible starting lineup:.

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Alhassane; Bernardeschi, Cambiaghi; Odgaard.

Udinese possible starting lineup:.

Okoye; Abankwah, Palma, Solet; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Zaniolo, Ekkelenkamp; Davis.

Bologna may be in fine form but they tend to falter on home turf, while Udinese are struggling to pick up points anywhere.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals than the Friulani, and the Rossoblu have kept just a single clean sheet, so a score-draw could be on the cards.

Barcelona vs. Villarreal: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 09:23, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:23.
  • Barcelona will resume their 2026-27 La Liga campaign with a home fixture against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon.
  • Hansi Flick's side are at the moment top of the La Liga table, boasting a record of 11 wins and one defeat from their 12 matches to collect 33 points, which has left them three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid at this stage of proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 09:23, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:23.

Barcelona will resume their 2026-27 La Liga campaign with a home fixture against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are at the moment top of the La Liga table, boasting a record of 11 wins and one defeat from their 12 matches to collect 33 points, which has left them three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid at this stage of proceedings.

Barcelona have won their last three games in all competitions, including a 2-1 success over Atletico Madrid in their last fixture before the November international break.

Villarreal, meanwhile, have a record of four wins, three draws and five defeats from their 12 league matches this season to collect 15 points.

The Yellow Submarine are right now eighth in the division, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record between Barcelona and Villarreal ahead of their clash at Camp Nou this weekend.

Barcelona have tackled Villarreal on 58 occasions throughout history, and they comfortably lead the head-to-head record, posting 36 wins to Villarreal's 12, while there have also been 10 draws.

Lionel Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having found the back of the net on 16 occasions against Villarreal during his time at Barcelona, while Neymar is second on nine.

As for the Yellow Submarine, former Manchester United and Atletico Madrid star Diego Forlan is their leading goalscorer against Barcelona, having netted five times against the Catalan outfit during his Villarreal career.

In La Liga, there have been 52 meetings, with Barcelona's winning 32 times to Villarreal's 11, while the points have been shared on nine occasions in Spain's top flight.

Villarreal incredibly recorded a 5-3 victory away to Barcelona in January 2024 and 3-2 win in May 2025, either side of a 5-1 triumph for the Catalan team in September 2024.

However, they were most recently downed 2-0 by La Blaugrana at Estadio de la Ceramica in December 2025, with centre-back Renato Veiga being sent off for a reckless tackle on Lamine Yamal, who went on to score the second for Hansi Flick's side.

Villarreal's last three wins over Barcelona have all come away from home, and they have not actually managed to beat the Catalan side in front of their own supporters since October 2007.

Barcelona's dominance in this fixture is perhaps best highlighted by the fact that they have won 12 of the last 15 La Liga meetings between the two clubs, even if Villarreal have enjoyed strong spells such as when they recorded three straight victories between April 2007 and March 2008.

The last meeting between the two sides took place at Camp Nou in February 2026, with Barcelona recording a 4-1 win.

Barcelona will now be looking to post a third straight victory over Villarreal.

AC Milan and Juventus are both keeping tabs on Benjamin Sesko’s situation at Manchester United, according to a report.

United paid around €80m to sign Sesko from RB Leipzig, hoping he would be the long-term fix for the No.9 position. Last season he performed reasonably well, scoring 11 goals in 30 Premier League games which was not bad for a 22-year-old in a upcoming league.

Recent findings suggest that this season, however, he is stuck on one goal in four league games, having spent time out injured too. With major changes at Old Trafford – including the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach – it is another blank slate for the squad.

For example, club captain Bruno Fernandes has been linked with a move to Milan. Now, according to journalist Alessandro Jacobone, a new idea has emerged for the centre-forward position, perhaps if the pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi does not go to plan.

“Juve and Milan are keeping an eye on things. But summer is the most realistic scenario. Benjamin Šeško could leave Manchester United, with Juventus and Milan having already made some preliminary enquiries to assess the financial feasibility of a potential move,” he said.

“For now, these are only preliminary discussions, useful for finding out the figures, conditions and possible deal structures. No concrete negotiations have been initiated.

Recent findings suggest that “Sources close to the player’s camp are also playing down the possibility of a transfer as early as January, making a potential move in the next summer window considerably more likely. One to watch.”.

Four of those 11 goals in his debut campaign came off the bench too as he developed a knack for being an impact substitute. This could give Milan food for thought, given they are looking for an alter-ego to Goncalo Ramos rather than someone to solely take over the striker role.

#26271. Breaking: The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1413 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1413 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’.

It is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

What unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign.

According to recent reports, utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

In a recent development, let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a latest four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the new head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

What would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

Both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen.

According to recent reports, scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

All of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a new generation of players.

It was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

His remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

There has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

In a recent development, there is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil new boss Pocognoli at Hampden.

Recent findings suggest that over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’.

That’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a upcoming four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

In a recent development, the whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

In a recent development, it is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a new head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Recent findings suggest that listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

But the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

In a recent development, things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign.

Industry observers note that all of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

Sources indicate that how must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

The captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

According to recent reports, there was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

But on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Industry observers note that steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs.

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

Industry observers note that those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

In a recent development, that feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

Recent findings suggest that we are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

Arsenal suffer huge early injury blows for Man City, Real Madrid as Mikel Arteta gives Bukayo Saka, Martin Zubimendi updates

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 10:00.
  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka will spend another four weeks on the sidelines with the quadriceps injury he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.
  • Saka's injury occurred in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Bundesliga champions on October 21, and Arteta immediately conceded at full time that the winger's problem looked severe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 10:00.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka will spend another four weeks on the sidelines with the quadriceps injury he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Saka's injury occurred in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Bundesliga champions on October 21, and Arteta immediately conceded at full time that the winger's problem looked severe.

Reports emerging soon after stated that Saka would miss between six and eight weeks, although Arsenal have been loath to put an exact timeframe on the Englishman's recovery just yet.

However, speaking to the media ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Newcastle United, Arteta admitted that Saka was only halfway into his recovery process and would spend the full eight weeks out.

According to recent reports, "We had another test. It looks like it’s going to be an eight week injury more or less. He’s four weeks in now," the Spaniard told reporters.

Saka missing another four weeks means that the 25-year-old is set to sit out another seven matches across all competitions, including a number of heavyweight fixtures.

Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League next Tuesday, before ending the month with a clash of the titans against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Saka is also expected to miss matches with Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in early December, and he will most likely be unavailable for the visit of Bournemouth on December 13 too.

However, the attacker could be fit to make his comeback against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on December 20, until when Noni Madueke and Max Dowman will provide cover.

Dowman will serve the third of his three-game domestic suspension against Newcastle this weekend, but Madueke has earned numerous plaudits in recent weeks, having scored against Slavia Prague in the Champions League before firing the effort that led to Martin Odegaard's winner against Hull City.

Saka will likely be one of two core members of Arsenal's title-winning team to miss matches against Tottenham and Real Madrid, as Arteta also delivered negative news on Martin Zubimendi.

The midfielder appeared to hurt his hamstring in Spain's 3-2 Nations League defeat to England during the international break, and he also faces around a month on the sidelines.

Industry observers note that "He has a problem in his hamstring. The scan indicates there is an injury there he will be out for a few weeks," Arteta added on Zubimendi.

However, the 27-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game this season and was always expected to lose out to Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes at St James' Park tomorrow.

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into gameweek 11 and are searching for their fourth successive win over Newcastle in the top flight.
